intent.raw_query: Portugal Algarve, $2200, beach holiday with wine tasting, September 2026 from London

experiences.name: Praia da Marinha Coastal Hike & Swim
experiences.description: Explore one of the Algarve's most stunning beaches, known for its dramatic golden limestone cliffs, sea caves, and crystal-clear turquoise waters. Hike the clifftop trail and descend to the secluded cove for a refreshing swim among natural rock arches.

experiences.name: Algarve Wine & Vineyard Tour
experiences.description: Visit local Algarve wineries such as Quinta dos Vales or Adega do Cantor near Guia, sampling regional varieties including Negra Mole and Arinto. Enjoy guided cellar tours, vineyard walks, and paired tastings of local cheeses and charcuterie with your wines.

experiences.name: Benagil Sea Cave Kayak Tour
experiences.description: Paddle by kayak through the iconic Benagil Cave, one of the world's most beautiful sea caves, accessible only from the water. A guided tour takes you through hidden grottos, sea arches, and secret beaches along the dramatic Algarve coastline.

experiences.name: Ria Formosa Natural Park Boat & Seafood Experience
experiences.description: Take a scenic boat tour through the Ria Formosa lagoon system, stopping at barrier islands like Ilha Deserta and Ilha do Farol. Enjoy freshly harvested oysters and clams directly from local fishermen, paired with a crisp local Vinho Verde.

experiences.name: Lagos Old Town Sunset Wine Bar Crawl
experiences.description: Wander through the charming cobblestone streets of Lagos historic center, stopping at curated wine bars to sample Alentejo and Algarve regional wines. End the evening at a clifftop viewpoint at Ponta da Piedade to watch the sun set over the Atlantic with a glass in hand.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Portugal Algarve
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Arrival day
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - Arrival day
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Faro Airport at 22:30 on flight UA. Take the affordable Proximo bus line (Line 16) or shared shuttle to Aegean Bliss Resort in the Algarve beachfront area. Check in, freshen up, and get settled into your room.

meals.breakfast: N/A
meals.lunch: N/A
meals.dinner: Grab a quick late-night snack at a 24-hour convenience store or vending machine near the airport or hotel lobby. Budget tip: pick up water and snacks for under €5.

day_by_day.notes: Flight arrives late at night. Keep Day 1 light — just focus on a smooth arrival and check-in. Confirm hotel shuttle availability in advance or pre-book a shared transfer for around €10-€15 per person. Set an alarm to start Day 2 refreshed.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up and enjoy your first Algarve morning. Take a leisurely walk along the beachfront promenade directly from the hotel. Explore Meia Praia or the nearest local beach — the calm September sea is perfect for an early morning swim or a barefoot stroll along the shoreline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head into the nearest town center (Lagos or Albufeira depending on hotel location) by local bus (under €2). Visit the free-to-explore old town streets, admire the traditional azulejo tile facades, and pop into the Mercado Municipal (local market) to sample fresh fruit and regional cheeses at very low cost.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the beachfront area and watch the stunning Algarve sunset from the beach. Explore the hotel surroundings and nearby esplanade.

meals.breakfast: Enjoy the hotel breakfast if included, or head to a local pastelaria (pastry shop) for a galão (milky coffee) and pastel de nata for under €3.
meals.lunch: Grab a prego no pão (beef sandwich) or bifanas from a local snack bar in town for €3-€5.
meals.dinner: Find a budget-friendly tasca (traditional tavern) near the beachfront. Order the prato do dia (dish of the day) which typically includes soup, main, and bread for €8-€10. Try grilled sardines or bacalhau (salted cod).

day_by_day.notes: September is shoulder season in the Algarve — weather is still warm (around 25-28°C), crowds are thinning, and prices are slightly lower than peak August. Perfect for budget travelers.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Praia da Marinha or Praia do Camilo (two of the Algarve's most scenic beaches with dramatic golden cliffs). Take a local bus or rent a bicycle from a nearby shop (€10-€15/day) to reach the beach. Spend the morning swimming, snorkeling, or simply relaxing on the sand.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the iconic Ponta da Piedade rock formations near Lagos — a free, breathtaking natural landmark with sea caves, grottos, and arches carved by the Atlantic. Walk the clifftop trails for free panoramic views. Optionally rent a kayak locally (€15-€20) to paddle through the sea caves.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through Lagos old town in the golden hour light. Browse the artisan craft stalls and street performers along Rua 25 de Abril.

meals.breakfast: Pastelaria breakfast: coffee and toasted bread with butter and jam (torrada) for €2-€3.
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic from the Mercado Municipal — fresh bread, local cheese, tomatoes, and fruit for under €5 total.
meals.dinner: Dine at a local restaurant in Lagos old town. Try cataplana (traditional Algarve seafood stew) at a budget tasca for €10-€12. Share a carafe of local house wine for €4-€5.

day_by_day.notes: Ponta da Piedade is free to visit on foot. The clifftop walk is about 1km and offers incredible photo opportunities. Wear comfortable shoes and bring sunscreen.

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning trip to Sagres, the southwestern tip of Portugal and Europe's 'Land's End'. Catch an early bus from Lagos (around €4 each way). Visit the imposing Fortaleza de Sagres (fortress) — entry is only €3. Explore the dramatic cliffs of Cabo de São Vicente, the most southwestern point of continental Europe.
day_by_day.afternoon: Relax at Praia do Martinhal or Praia de Sagres — quieter, wilder Atlantic beaches with a raw, unspoiled feel. The water is cooler here due to Atlantic currents but the scenery is spectacular.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel area by bus. Enjoy a quiet evening walk along your local beachfront promenade as the sun sets.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast at the hotel or a local café before catching the bus — coffee and pastry for €2-€3.
meals.lunch: Eat at a simple restaurant in Sagres village — grilled fish of the day with salad and bread for €9-€11.
meals.dinner: Cook a simple meal using ingredients from a local supermarket (Pingo Doce or Lidl) — pasta, canned tuna, vegetables for under €5. Great budget hack for one evening.

day_by_day.notes: Sagres has a raw, windswept beauty that's very different from the eastern Algarve. The fortress is historically significant as the site where Prince Henry the Navigator planned his Age of Discovery expeditions. Bus schedules from Lagos to Sagres run several times daily.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicate the morning to a wine tasting experience. Visit a local Algarve wine estate — the Algarve wine region (DOC Algarve) produces excellent reds, whites, and rosés. Look for Quinta dos Vales or Adega do Cantor near Lagoa/Silves. Some estates offer free or low-cost tastings (€5-€10) when you visit directly.
day_by_day.afternoon: After wine tasting, explore the medieval town of Silves — the ancient Moorish capital of the Algarve. Visit the impressive red sandstone Castelo de Silves (€3 entry) and the Gothic Cathedral of Silves (free). Wander the charming cobblestone streets.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel area and relax on the beach for the evening golden hour.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or local café — galão and croissant for €3.
meals.lunch: Have lunch at the wine estate if they offer it (many do for €10-€15), or grab a meal in Silves town — a simple restaurant near the castle serves local food for €8-€10.
meals.dinner: Try a local beach bar restaurant (chiringuito) near the hotel for grilled fish or a mixed grill plate with a cold Sagres beer for €10-€12.

day_by_day.notes: Book wine estate visits in advance, especially for guided tours. Some estates offer free tastings with purchase of a bottle. The Algarve produces surprisingly good wines that are less well-known internationally, making them excellent value.

day_by_day.morning: Beach day at Meia Praia — one of the longest beaches in the Algarve (4km of golden sand). Perfect for a long morning walk, swimming, and sunbathing. Bring snorkeling gear if you have it — the clear September waters are ideal.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a stand-up paddleboard (SUP) or kayak from a local beach rental shop (€10-€15/hour) and explore the coastline from the water. Alternatively, join a free beach volleyball game or simply relax and read.
day_by_day.evening: Head to a local miradouro (viewpoint) to watch the sunset over the Atlantic. Many are free and accessible by foot or bicycle.

meals.breakfast: Supermarket breakfast on the beach — yogurt, fruit, and bread bought the evening before for under €4.
meals.lunch: Beach snack bar — toasted sandwich (tosta mista) and fresh orange juice for €5-€6.
meals.dinner: Visit a local mercado de peixe (fish market) or a simple seafood restaurant. Order grilled dourada (sea bream) or robalo (sea bass) with potatoes and salad for €10-€13.

day_by_day.notes: September sea temperatures in the Algarve average around 22-24°C — warm enough for comfortable swimming. Beach rental equipment prices drop in September compared to peak season.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to Portimão and Ferragudo. Explore the charming fishing village of Ferragudo — cross the Arade River by local ferry (€1-€2 each way) from Portimão. Wander Ferragudo's whitewashed streets, visit the 16th-century Castelo de São João do Arade (exterior free), and enjoy the village atmosphere.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Praia da Rocha in Portimão — one of the Algarve's most famous beaches with impressive ochre-colored cliffs. Explore the clifftop walkway for free panoramic views. Browse the local shops and esplanade.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel. Enjoy a relaxed evening at a local beach bar with a sundowner drink.

meals.breakfast: Coffee and pastel de nata at a local pastelaria for €2.
meals.lunch: Eat at a local restaurant in Ferragudo — fresh grilled fish or seafood rice for €10-€12. Ferragudo is less touristy than Portimão so prices are lower.
meals.dinner: Budget supermarket dinner at the hotel or a simple takeaway pizza from a local pizzeria for €7-€9.

day_by_day.notes: Ferragudo is a hidden gem that many tourists skip in favor of busier Portimão. It has a more authentic Portuguese village feel. The ferry crossing is a fun and cheap way to travel between the two towns.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Algar Seco rock formations in Carvoeiro — a stunning natural geological wonder of eroded limestone rocks, sea arches, and tidal pools. Free to visit and walk around. The coastal boardwalk (passadiço) offers spectacular views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the village of Carvoeiro itself — a picturesque whitewashed fishing village with a small beach nestled between cliffs. Browse local craft shops and enjoy the relaxed atmosphere. Visit Praia de Carvoeiro for an afternoon swim.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel area. Enjoy a leisurely evening walk along the beachfront.

meals.breakfast: Local café breakfast in Carvoeiro — coffee and toast for €3.
meals.lunch: Grab a fresh sandwich or bifana from a snack bar in Carvoeiro for €3-€5.
meals.dinner: Try a traditional Portuguese restaurant near the hotel. Order arroz de marisco (seafood rice) — a hearty, flavorful dish for €12-€14. Share between two for better value.

day_by_day.notes: Algar Seco is best visited in the morning when the light is perfect for photography. Wear non-slip shoes as the rocks can be slippery. The area is free to access.

day_by_day.morning: Second wine tasting experience — visit the Lagoa wine cooperative (Adega Cooperativa de Lagoa), one of the oldest and most respected wine producers in the Algarve. They offer affordable tastings of their regional wines including the local Negra Mole and Crato Branco grape varieties. Entry and tasting from €5.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the town of Lagoa — a traditional Algarve market town with a beautiful parish church and a relaxed local atmosphere away from tourist crowds. Visit the weekly market if timing aligns. Browse local shops for affordable Portuguese wine to take home.
day_by_day.evening: Head back to the beachfront for a sunset swim or a walk along the shore.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or pastelaria stop for €3.
meals.lunch: Eat at a local tasca in Lagoa town — locals eat here, prices are low. A full lunch with wine for €8-€10.
meals.dinner: Cook at the hotel using local market ingredients — Portuguese-style omelette with local chouriço and vegetables for under €5.

day_by_day.notes: Lagoa is less visited by tourists but offers an authentic glimpse into everyday Algarve life. The wine cooperative is a great place to buy quality local wine at producer prices — much cheaper than tourist shops.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the stunning Benagil Sea Cave — one of the most photographed natural wonders in Portugal. Take a local kayak or paddleboard tour from Praia de Benagil (€15-€20) to enter the famous cave with its natural skylight ceiling, or hire a kayak independently (€10-€15/hour). Book early morning to avoid crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Relax at Praia de Benagil or the nearby Praia do Carvalho (accessible via a short tunnel through the cliff — free). These are among the most beautiful beaches in the Algarve.
day_by_day.evening: Head back to the hotel and enjoy a relaxed evening at a nearby restaurant or beach bar.

meals.breakfast: Early start — grab a coffee and pastry to go from a nearby café for €2-€3.
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic to enjoy on the beach — bread, local cheese, olives, and fruit from a supermarket for €5-€6.
meals.dinner: Treat yourself slightly tonight — a nice seafood dinner at a local restaurant near the hotel. Fresh grilled prawns or a cataplana for €12-€15. Well-deserved after a full day.

day_by_day.notes: The Benagil Cave can only be entered from the water — you cannot walk in from the beach. Book kayak or boat tours in advance as they fill up quickly even in September. Go early morning (before 9am) for the best light and fewest crowds.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Albufeira — the Algarve's most famous resort town. Explore the historic old town (Albufeira Velha) which retains its original Moorish street layout. Visit the free Museu Municipal de Arqueologia to learn about the region's history. Walk along the Fisherman's Beach (Praia dos Pescadores).
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the free elevator (ascensor) up the cliff for views over Albufeira. Explore the clifftop esplanade and Praia do Peneco. Browse the local market stalls for affordable souvenirs — hand-painted ceramics, cork products, and local preserves.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy Albufeira's lively but affordable evening atmosphere in the old town. Many bars offer happy hour deals. Return to hotel by bus.

meals.breakfast: Café breakfast in Albufeira old town for €3.
meals.lunch: Find a local workers' restaurant (restaurante popular) away from the main tourist strip — full lunch menu for €7-€9.
meals.dinner: Try a local churrasqueira (charcoal grill restaurant) in Albufeira — half a grilled chicken with chips and salad for €8-€10. Excellent value and delicious.

day_by_day.notes: Albufeira has a reputation for being touristy and expensive on the strip, but the old town is genuinely charming and more affordable. Avoid restaurants on the main tourist strip and walk one or two streets back for much better prices.

day_by_day.morning: Spend a final full beach morning at your favorite beach discovered during the trip. Take a long swim, collect shells, and soak in the last of the Algarve sunshine. Reflect on the trip over a coffee at a beach bar.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local mercado or farmers market for last-minute souvenir shopping — local honey, almond products (the Algarve is famous for almonds), medronho (local firewater brandy), and affordable Portuguese wine make excellent budget gifts.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell sunset walk along the beachfront promenade. Toast the trip with a glass of local Algarve wine or a cold beer at a beach bar.

meals.breakfast: Relaxed hotel breakfast or a final pastelaria visit — enjoy a slow coffee and pastel de nata.
meals.lunch: Beach snack bar lunch — fresh grilled sardines on bread (sardinhas assadas) with a cold drink for €6-€8. A classic Algarve farewell lunch.
meals.dinner: Final dinner at a local restaurant near the hotel. Splurge slightly on a special meal — fresh grilled fish, local wine, and a sobremesa (dessert) like tarte de amêndoa (almond tart) for €15-€18. A fitting farewell to the Algarve.

day_by_day.notes: Use this day to do any last-minute packing and prepare for departure. Check your flight details and arrange transport to the airport in advance. Confirm bus or shuttle schedules for the next morning.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in the Algarve. Enjoy a leisurely last breakfast. Take one final walk to the beach for a goodbye look at the Atlantic Ocean. Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort as per checkout time (typically 11:00-12:00).
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure flight time, either head directly to Faro Airport or spend remaining time in Faro city — visit the free Arco da Vila (old city gate), the historic old town (Cidade Velha), and the beautiful Faro Cathedral (€3 entry) if time allows.
day_by_day.evening: Depart from Faro Airport. Take the Proximo bus Line 16 from Faro city center to the airport (€2.35) or a pre-booked shared shuttle. Arrive at the airport with plenty of time for check-in.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast or a last café stop — enjoy a galão and pastel de nata one more time for €3.
meals.lunch: Light lunch in Faro old town if time allows — a simple sandwich or soup at a local café for €4-€6.
meals.dinner: Airport meal or on-flight dining. Budget tip: bring snacks purchased at a local supermarket before heading to the airport to avoid expensive airport food prices.

day_by_day.notes: Budget summary for the 13-day trip: Accommodation at Aegean Bliss Resort (pre-booked), daily meals averaging €15-€20/day, local transport €2-€5/day, activities and entrance fees averaging €5-€10/day, wine tastings €5-€10 per session. Total estimated daily budget excluding accommodation: €30-€40/day. Total trip activities and food budget approximately €390-€520 for 13 days — very achievable for a budget-conscious traveler in the Algarve.

trip_options.title: Classic Portugal Algarve Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

experiences.name: Praia da Marinha Coastal Hike & Swim
experiences.description: Explore one of the Algarve's most stunning beaches, known for its dramatic golden limestone cliffs, sea caves, and crystal-clear turquoise waters. Hike the clifftop trail and descend to the secluded cove for a refreshing swim among natural rock arches.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Late arrival day
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - Late arrival day
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Faro Airport at 22:30 on flight UA. Transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort in Beachfront Algarve (~45 min drive). Check in, freshen up, and unwind at the hotel bar for a welcome drink.

meals.breakfast: N/A
meals.lunch: N/A
meals.dinner: Light late-night snack at the hotel bar or room service upon arrival

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange airport transfer with the resort for a smooth arrival. Pack a light snack for the journey in case airport food options are limited at that hour.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the resort. Spend the late morning exploring the resort's beachfront — take a gentle walk along the shoreline to get your bearings and soak in the Algarve atmosphere.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the nearby local beach for an afternoon of relaxation. Rent a sun lounger and umbrella, take a swim in the warm September Atlantic waters, and explore the coastal rock formations on foot.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll into the nearest town center for dinner at a traditional Portuguese restaurant. Try grilled fish (peixe grelhado) and a glass of local Alentejo white wine. Return to the resort for an early night to recover from travel.

meals.breakfast: Buffet breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort (included or modest surcharge)
meals.lunch: Light snack at the beach — grab pastéis de nata and fresh juice from a nearby café
meals.dinner: O Zé da Praia or similar local tasca — grilled sea bream, salad, and house wine (~€25–35 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Day 2 is intentionally relaxed to recover from travel. Keep activities low-key and close to the resort.

day_by_day.morning: Praia da Marinha Coastal Hike & Swim: Depart early for one of the Algarve's most iconic beaches. Walk the dramatic clifftop trail above golden limestone arches, sea caves, and turquoise coves. The hike is approximately 4 km round trip with stunning photo opportunities.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend to Praia da Marinha beach for a swim in the crystal-clear waters. Explore the sea caves and rock arches by swimming or renting a kayak from a local operator on the beach. Enjoy the dramatic scenery of the golden cliffs up close.
day_by_day.evening: Drive to Carvoeiro village for dinner. Browse the charming whitewashed streets before settling into a seafood restaurant overlooking the beach. Try cataplana de marisco (seafood stew) — a regional Algarve specialty.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before departure
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or snacks at the beach — pick up local bread, cheese, and charcuterie from a nearby market
meals.dinner: Restaurante O Castelo in Carvoeiro — cataplana de marisco and Vinho Verde (~€30–40 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Wear sturdy shoes for the coastal hike. Bring sunscreen, water, and a hat. September water temperatures are ideal (~22°C). Arrive at Praia da Marinha early to secure parking and avoid crowds.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Silves — the ancient Moorish capital of the Algarve. Explore the impressive red sandstone Silves Castle (Castelo de Silves) with panoramic views over orange groves and the Arade River. Walk through the medieval old town and visit the Gothic Cathedral.
day_by_day.afternoon: Wine tasting experience in the Silves region. Visit a local quinta (wine estate) such as Quinta dos Vales or Quinta do Barradas for a guided tour of the vineyards and a tasting of Algarve regional wines, including the distinctive Negra Mole grape variety.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Silves at a traditional restaurant in the historic center. Try espetada (meat skewers) or arroz de lingueirão (razor clam rice) paired with a bottle of local red wine discovered during the afternoon tasting.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a café in Silves town center — soup and sandwich (~€10–12 per person)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Marisqueira Rui in Silves — regional seafood and Algarve wines (~€28–38 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book the wine tasting in advance. Quinta dos Vales offers tastings from ~€15–25 per person including 4–6 wines. Silves is approximately 30–40 minutes from most Algarve beachfront resorts.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Praia da Rocha in Portimão — one of the Algarve's most famous beaches with wide golden sands and impressive cliff formations. Walk the clifftop promenade and explore the fortress ruins overlooking the beach.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a scenic boat trip from Portimão marina along the coastline to explore sea caves, grottos, and hidden beaches inaccessible by land. Most tours last 2–3 hours and include stops for swimming.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Portimão — famous for its grilled sardines (sardinhas assadas). Head to the riverside area near the old fish market for authentic grilled sardines at one of the local restaurants. Pair with local beer or a crisp white wine.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort
meals.lunch: Snack on the boat or grab a bifana (pork sandwich) from a local café in Portimão
meals.dinner: Taberna da Maré or similar riverside restaurant in Portimão — grilled sardines, potatoes, and salad (~€20–28 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Boat trips depart regularly from Portimão marina. Book in advance during September as tours can fill up. Cost is approximately €20–30 per person. Bring motion sickness tablets if needed.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Lagos — one of the most charming towns in the Algarve. Explore the historic old town, walk the ancient city walls, and visit the Igreja de Santo António with its stunning gilded baroque interior.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the famous Ponta da Piedade — a breathtaking series of golden rock formations, sea arches, and grottos just south of Lagos. Walk the clifftop paths for spectacular views, then kayak or take a small boat into the sea caves below.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Lagos town center. The vibrant restaurant scene offers excellent mid-range options. Try amêijoas à bulhão pato (clams in garlic and white wine) followed by grilled fish. Enjoy the lively evening atmosphere in the historic center.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort
meals.lunch: Lunch at a restaurant near Ponta da Piedade or a picnic on the cliffs with supplies from Lagos market
meals.dinner: Restaurante Adega da Marina in Lagos — clams, grilled fish, and local wine (~€28–38 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Lagos is approximately 30–45 minutes from most Algarve beachfront resorts. Ponta da Piedade boat tours cost ~€15–20 per person. The clifftop walk is free and stunning even without the boat.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and relaxation day at the resort. Enjoy a leisurely morning at the pool or beach. Try a water sport offered by the resort — paddleboarding or snorkeling in the calm September waters.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local wine shop or deli in the nearest town to stock up on Algarve wines, local honey, fig products, and almond sweets (Dom Rodrigos) — the region's most famous confection. Browse the local market if available.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the resort bar followed by a special dinner at the resort restaurant. Treat yourself to a slightly elevated meal — try fresh lobster or premium grilled fish with a bottle of Algarve wine selected from your afternoon shopping.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely breakfast at the resort
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the resort pool bar — salads, sandwiches, and fresh juices
meals.dinner: Resort restaurant — splurge slightly on fresh lobster or premium catch of the day (~€35–50 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Mid-trip rest day is important for recharging. Use this day to do laundry, plan the second week, and make any remaining reservations for wine tastings or boat trips.

day_by_day.morning: Drive east to visit Albufeira — the Algarve's most popular resort town. Explore the charming old town (Albufeira Velha) with its whitewashed buildings, narrow streets, and beautiful main square. Visit the local fish market.
day_by_day.afternoon: Praia do Olhos de Água — a quieter, more authentic fishing village beach east of Albufeira. Swim, snorkel, and explore the small caves and rock pools. Watch local fishermen bring in their catch in the late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Albufeira's old town. The area has excellent mid-range seafood restaurants away from the tourist strip. Try grilled octopus (polvo grelhado) — a local favorite — with a glass of chilled rosé.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood lunch at a beachside restaurant in Olhos de Água — grilled fish and salad (~€18–25 per person)
meals.dinner: Restaurante A Ruína in Albufeira old town — octopus, seafood rice, and local wine (~€28–38 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Albufeira can be busy even in September. Visit the old town in the morning before the crowds build. Park at the main car park and walk into the historic center.

day_by_day.morning: Wine tasting day trip to the Alentejo region — the most celebrated wine region near the Algarve. Drive approximately 1.5 hours north to Vidigueira or Reguengos de Monsaraz. Visit Herdade do Esporão or Adega Mayor for a world-class winery tour.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the wine experience with a second tasting at a boutique quinta. Explore the rolling cork oak and olive tree landscapes of the Alentejo. Visit the medieval village of Monsaraz — a stunning hilltop fortress town with panoramic views over the Alqueva reservoir.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Monsaraz or on the way back through Évora if time permits. Try Alentejo specialties — migas (bread-based dish), black pork (porco preto), and Alentejo wines. Return to the resort in the evening.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch at the winery restaurant or a local tasca in Vidigueira (~€20–30 per person)
meals.dinner: Restaurant in Monsaraz or a roadside tasca on the return journey — Alentejo pork and regional wine (~€25–35 per person)

day_by_day.notes: This is a full-day excursion — depart by 8:30 AM. Book winery tours in advance. Esporão offers excellent guided tours with tastings from ~€15–25 per person. Designate a driver or consider a guided wine tour from the resort.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Loulé — the Algarve's most authentic inland market town. Visit the spectacular covered market (Mercado de Loulé) housed in a Moorish-style building. Browse fresh produce, local cheeses, smoked meats, honey, and crafts. Visit the Loulé Castle.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Praia de Quarteira or Praia de Vilamoura for an afternoon beach session. The beaches here are wide, long, and backed by a lively promenade. Take a walk along the Vilamoura marina and admire the luxury yachts.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at the Vilamoura marina — excellent mid-range restaurants line the waterfront. Try grilled tiger prawns (gambas grelhadas) or a mixed seafood platter with a bottle of Algarve white wine while watching the boats.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort
meals.lunch: Lunch at Loulé market — pick up local produce, olives, cheese, and bread for a market picnic (~€10–15 per person)
meals.dinner: Marina restaurant in Vilamoura — seafood platter and local wine (~€30–40 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Loulé market is best visited in the morning when it is most lively. The market is open Monday to Saturday. Pick up local almond products and carob sweets as souvenirs.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Tavira — widely considered the most beautiful town in the Algarve. Cross the seven-arched Roman bridge over the Gilão River, explore the castle ruins, and visit the stunning Igreja da Misericórdia with its ornate portal.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the short ferry crossing to Ilha de Tavira — a pristine barrier island beach within the Ria Formosa Natural Park. The beach is wild, unspoiled, and perfect for swimming and walking. September crowds are minimal.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Tavira town center. The town has a sophisticated dining scene. Try tuna (atum) — a local specialty in eastern Algarve — prepared as a steak or in a traditional cataplana. Pair with a crisp Algarve white wine.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort
meals.lunch: Beach bar lunch on Ilha de Tavira — grilled fish and salad (~€15–20 per person)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Aquasul in Tavira — tuna steak or cataplana with local wine (~€28–38 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Tavira is approximately 45–60 minutes east of central Algarve. The ferry to Ilha de Tavira runs regularly and costs ~€2–3 return. The island beach is a highlight — allow at least 2–3 hours.

day_by_day.morning: Final wine tasting experience — visit a local Algarve winery closer to the resort. Quinta do Barranco Longo or Quinta da Penina offer excellent local tastings. Focus on buying favorite bottles to take home as gifts or personal souvenirs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to your favorite beach from the trip for a final long swim and beach session. Alternatively, try a new beach such as Praia de Benagil — famous for the stunning Benagil Cave accessible by kayak or boat tour.
day_by_day.evening: Special farewell dinner at a top-rated local restaurant. Splurge slightly for the final evening — try a tasting menu or chef's special at a well-regarded Algarve restaurant. Celebrate the trip with a bottle of premium Alentejo red wine.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort
meals.lunch: Light lunch after the winery visit — soup and local bread at a café
meals.dinner: Vila Joya or similar acclaimed restaurant (book well in advance) OR a quality local restaurant — tasting menu or premium seafood (~€45–65 per person for a special farewell)

day_by_day.notes: Book the farewell dinner well in advance, especially for higher-end restaurants. Pack wine purchases carefully for the flight home — use bubble wrap or a wine travel bag. Check airline liquid/bottle restrictions.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning at the resort. Enjoy a last leisurely breakfast and a final walk along the beach. Pack and check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. Store luggage with the concierge if the flight is later in the day.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on flight time, enjoy a final coffee and pastel de nata at a local café, or browse any remaining shops for last-minute souvenirs — local ceramics, azulejos (painted tiles), almond sweets, and bottled olive oil make excellent gifts.
day_by_day.evening: Transfer to Faro Airport for departure. Reflect on 13 wonderful days exploring the beaches, wines, and culture of the Algarve.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast — savor it!
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a café near the resort or at Faro Airport (~€12–18 per person)
meals.dinner: Airport dining or in-flight meal

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2 hours before departure for airport check-in and security. Faro Airport is generally efficient but can be busy in September. Confirm transfer booking the night before.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Portugal Algarve Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Praia da Marinha Coastal Hike & Swim
experiences.description: Explore one of the Algarve's most stunning beaches, known for its dramatic golden limestone cliffs, sea caves, and crystal-clear turquoise waters. Hike the clifftop trail and descend to the secluded cove for a refreshing swim among natural rock arches.

experiences.name: Algarve Wine & Vineyard Tour
experiences.description: Visit local Algarve wineries such as Quinta dos Vales or Adega do Cantor near Guia, sampling regional varieties including Negra Mole and Arinto. Enjoy guided cellar tours, vineyard walks, and paired tastings of local cheeses and charcuterie with your wines.

experiences.name: Benagil Sea Cave Kayak Tour
experiences.description: Paddle by kayak through the iconic Benagil Cave, one of the world's most beautiful sea caves, accessible only from the water. A guided tour takes you through hidden grottos, sea arches, and secret beaches along the dramatic Algarve coastline.

experiences.name: Ria Formosa Natural Park Boat & Seafood Experience
experiences.description: Take a scenic boat tour through the Ria Formosa lagoon system, stopping at barrier islands like Ilha Deserta and Ilha do Farol. Enjoy freshly harvested oysters and clams directly from local fishermen, paired with a crisp local Vinho Verde.

experiences.name: Lagos Old Town Sunset Wine Bar Crawl
experiences.description: Wander through the charming cobblestone streets of Lagos historic center, stopping at curated wine bars to sample Alentejo and Algarve regional wines. End the evening at a clifftop viewpoint at Ponta da Piedade to watch the sun set over the Atlantic with a glass in hand.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late night arrival
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — late night arrival
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Faro Airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. Private luxury transfer arranged to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check-in, unwind with a welcome drink at the resort's bar, and settle into your beachfront suite.

meals.breakfast: N/A
meals.lunch: N/A
meals.dinner: Light late-night welcome platter and champagne provided by the resort upon arrival

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange private airport transfer with the resort concierge. Request early check-in preparation so the room is fully ready upon arrival. Keep this evening completely relaxed to recover from travel.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely start — enjoy a lavish breakfast at the resort's beachfront restaurant. Take a slow morning stroll along the resort's private beach, acclimatizing to the Algarve's stunning coastline and warm September sun.
day_by_day.afternoon: Praia da Marinha Coastal Hike & Swim: Head to one of the Algarve's most celebrated beaches, Praia da Marinha, featuring dramatic golden limestone cliffs, hidden grottos, and crystal-clear turquoise waters. Enjoy a guided coastal hike along the clifftop trails followed by a refreshing swim in the sheltered coves below.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a sunset cocktail on your private terrace or at the infinity pool bar overlooking the Atlantic. Enjoy a refined dinner at the resort's signature fine-dining restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet breakfast buffet at the Aegean Bliss Resort beachfront restaurant — fresh pastries, local cheeses, charcuterie, eggs to order, and freshly squeezed orange juice
meals.lunch: Picnic-style premium lunch arranged by the resort concierge to enjoy at Praia da Marinha — chilled rosé, artisan sandwiches, local cheeses, and seasonal fruit
meals.dinner: Dinner at the resort's signature restaurant — try the grilled sea bass with Algarve herb oil and a bottle of Alentejo white wine

day_by_day.notes: Praia da Marinha is approximately 20–30 minutes from most Algarve resort areas. Wear comfortable hiking shoes and bring sunscreen. September waters are warm and ideal for swimming.

day_by_day.morning: Benagil Sea Cave Kayak Tour: Embark on an exclusive private kayak tour to the world-famous Benagil Cave. Paddle through dramatic sea arches and coastal rock formations, entering the cathedral-like interior of the cave illuminated by natural light from above. A truly once-in-a-lifetime Algarve experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the kayak tour, relax on Praia de Benagil beach. Arrange a private yacht charter for a 2-hour afternoon cruise along the Algarve's spectacular coastline, sipping chilled Vinho Verde on deck while admiring the golden cliffs from the sea.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset aperitivo hour at the resort pool bar. Dine at a premium local seafood restaurant in Carvoeiro village — a charming fishing village just minutes from the resort.

meals.breakfast: À la carte breakfast at the resort — smoked salmon eggs benedict, fresh tropical fruit, and artisan coffee
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood lunch at a beachside restaurant near Benagil — grilled octopus, gambas al ajillo, and local white wine
meals.dinner: Dinner at Restaurante O Castelo in Carvoeiro or equivalent — whole grilled lobster, cataplana de marisco (seafood stew), and a premium Algarve white wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Book the Benagil kayak tour in advance as spots fill quickly, especially in September. Opt for a private guided tour for the most luxurious experience. The kayak tour is best done in the morning when seas are calmest.

day_by_day.morning: Algarve Wine & Vineyard Tour — Morning Session: Begin the day with a private chauffeured wine tour to Quinta dos Vales, one of the Algarve's most prestigious estates near Estômbar. Enjoy an exclusive guided tour of the vineyards and wine cellars, learning about the region's unique terroir and winemaking traditions.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the wine tour to Adega do Cantor near Guia — the celebrated winery associated with Sir Cliff Richard. Enjoy an intimate tasting of their award-winning Vida Nova and Onda Nova labels paired with local charcuterie, cheeses, and artisan breads in the estate's elegant tasting room.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort refreshed. Enjoy a relaxing spa treatment at the resort's luxury spa — choose from a signature Algarve citrus massage or a sea salt body scrub. End the evening with a candlelit dinner at the resort.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — fresh-baked croissants, local honey, yogurt with Algarve almonds and figs, and a selection of fine teas and coffees
meals.lunch: Wine-paired lunch at Quinta dos Vales estate — a curated tasting menu of local Algarvian flavors matched with their finest reserve wines
meals.dinner: Candlelit dinner at the resort's fine-dining terrace — duck rice with Algarve orange sauce and a glass of Quinta dos Vales Reserva red

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book the private wine tour through the resort concierge for a fully personalized experience with a dedicated sommelier guide. September is harvest season in the Algarve — you may have the opportunity to see or participate in the grape harvest.

day_by_day.morning: Ria Formosa Natural Park Boat & Seafood Experience — Morning Departure: Take a private luxury boat tour through the stunning Ria Formosa lagoon system, a UNESCO-listed natural park. Glide through tranquil waterways, spot flamingos and other migratory birds, and stop at pristine barrier islands like Ilha Deserta.
day_by_day.afternoon: Disembark on one of the barrier islands for a long, leisurely seafood lunch and an afternoon of relaxation on the unspoiled white-sand beaches of the Ria Formosa. Swim in the calm, shallow lagoon waters — ideal for a tranquil afternoon away from the crowds.
day_by_day.evening: Private transfer back to the resort. Enjoy sunset cocktails on your suite's private terrace. Dine at a premium restaurant in Faro's historic old town, exploring the charming walled city by night.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — full Portuguese spread with fresh pastéis de nata, local jams, cold cuts, and freshly squeezed juices
meals.lunch: Premium seafood lunch on Ilha Deserta at Restaurante Estaminé — oysters, clams, grilled fish of the day, and chilled local white wine with views over the lagoon
meals.dinner: Dinner at Restaurante São Pedro in Faro or equivalent — traditional Algarvian cataplana, fresh prawns, and a curated Portuguese wine list

day_by_day.notes: The Ria Formosa boat tour departs from Faro or Olhão — approximately 40–50 minutes from the resort. Bring a hat, sunscreen, and light layers as sea breezes can be refreshing. September is an excellent month for birdwatching in the lagoon.

day_by_day.morning: Leisure morning at the resort. Enjoy the infinity pool, beachfront loungers, or a private yoga session arranged by the resort on the beach at sunrise. This is a perfect day to recharge mid-trip.
day_by_day.afternoon: Lagos Old Town Sunset Wine Bar Crawl — Afternoon Exploration: Head to the historic city of Lagos (approximately 45 minutes west) for an afternoon of exploration. Wander through the charming cobblestone streets, visit the Ponta da Piedade rock formations, and begin an early evening curated wine bar crawl through Lagos' vibrant old town.
day_by_day.evening: Continue the Lagos wine bar crawl into the evening — sample premium Portuguese wines, local craft gins, and Algarvian medronho brandy at carefully selected boutique wine bars. Enjoy dinner in Lagos before a private transfer back to the resort.

meals.breakfast: In-suite breakfast delivered to your private terrace — freshly baked bread, smoked salmon, soft-boiled eggs, fresh fruit platter, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Light poolside lunch at the resort — grilled sea bream, fresh salad, and a glass of chilled Alvarinho
meals.dinner: Dinner at No Pátio restaurant in Lagos or equivalent — tuna tataki with Algarvian herbs, grilled black pork secreto, and a premium Douro red wine

day_by_day.notes: Lagos is approximately 45 minutes west of central Algarve. Arrange a private driver for the evening so you can fully enjoy the wine bar crawl without concern. Ponta da Piedade is best visited in the late afternoon for golden hour light on the rock formations.

day_by_day.morning: Private sunrise beach walk along the resort's beachfront. Followed by a world-class spa morning — indulge in a 90-minute couples' or solo treatment at the resort spa, choosing from hot stone massage, thalassotherapy, or a premium facial using Algarvian botanical ingredients.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the local area around the resort on a private e-bike tour along the coastal cliffs and countryside. Visit a local market or artisan shop to pick up handcrafted Algarvian ceramics, local honey, and premium cork products as souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Private sunset catamaran cruise along the Algarve coastline — champagne, canapés, and breathtaking views of the golden cliffs at dusk. Return to the resort for a late dinner.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast buffet — focus on local Algarvian specialties: carob bread, fig preserves, fresh almonds, and local cheeses
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic basket prepared by the resort chef, enjoyed at a scenic clifftop viewpoint during the e-bike tour
meals.dinner: Late dinner at the resort's terrace restaurant — slow-roasted lamb with rosemary and Algarve orange, paired with a Herdade do Esporão Reserva red

day_by_day.notes: Book the sunset catamaran cruise through the resort concierge for a private charter experience. September evenings are warm and perfect for an open-air sunset cruise. The spa is best booked at least 24 hours in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Sagres and Cabo de São Vicente — the southwestern-most tip of continental Europe. Explore the dramatic windswept cliffs, the historic Sagres Fortress, and the iconic lighthouse at Cabo de São Vicente. A powerful and awe-inspiring natural landmark.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the charming village of Sagres and visit Praia do Tonel, a spectacular and relatively uncrowded beach beloved by surfers. Enjoy a leisurely afternoon walk along the dramatic Atlantic coastline.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Sagres at a premium seafood restaurant before private transfer back to the resort. Alternatively, return to the resort for a relaxed evening at the beach bar watching the stars.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — full à la carte service with eggs Benedict, smoked swordfish, and freshly pressed juices
meals.lunch: Lunch at A Sagres restaurant or equivalent in Sagres village — fresh grilled tuna, local barnacles (percebes), and a crisp Vinho Verde
meals.dinner: Dinner at Restaurante Bossa Nova in Sagres or equivalent — grilled monkfish, prawns in garlic butter, and local house wine

day_by_day.notes: Sagres is approximately 1 hour 15 minutes west of the central Algarve. Arrange a private chauffeured day trip. The area around Cabo de São Vicente can be windy even in September — bring a light layer. This is one of the most dramatic and memorable excursions in the entire Algarve region.

day_by_day.morning: Return to Praia da Marinha for a more relaxed morning — rent a private sea kayak or stand-up paddleboard to explore the coastal sea caves and arches at your own pace. The calm September waters make this ideal for independent exploration.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the charming hilltop village of Alte, often called the prettiest village in the Algarve. Stroll through whitewashed streets, visit the 16th-century church, and enjoy the natural spring and traditional atmosphere far from the tourist crowds.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a private in-suite dinner experience — arrange with the resort concierge for a personal chef to prepare a bespoke Algarvian tasting menu on your private terrace, paired with wines selected by the resort sommelier.

meals.breakfast: In-suite breakfast — continental spread with fresh pastries, local honey, fruit, and specialty Portuguese coffee
meals.lunch: Traditional lunch at a local tasca in Alte village — piri piri chicken, caldo verde soup, local bread, and house red wine
meals.dinner: Private in-suite chef's tasting menu on your terrace — 5-course Algarvian menu featuring local seafood, black pork, almond desserts, and a curated wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: The private in-suite dinner experience should be booked 48 hours in advance through the resort concierge. Alte is approximately 40 minutes inland from the coast — a wonderful contrast to the beachside days and highly recommended for experiencing authentic Algarve culture.

day_by_day.morning: Full resort leisure morning — sleep in, enjoy the pool, or take a morning yoga or Pilates class on the beach. This is a dedicated relaxation day to recharge before the final days of the trip.
day_by_day.afternoon: Algarve Wine & Vineyard Tour — Second Visit: Return to the wine region for an afternoon visit to a different estate — explore Quinta da Penina or Herdade dos Grous near Albufeira. Enjoy a private barrel tasting and meet the winemaker for an exclusive behind-the-scenes experience.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the resort's rooftop or infinity pool bar. Dinner at a premium restaurant in Albufeira's old town — a vibrant and characterful dining scene just minutes from the resort.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely poolside breakfast at the resort — smashed avocado toast, poached eggs, smoked salmon, and freshly squeezed orange juice
meals.lunch: Wine estate lunch — estate-prepared tapas of local charcuterie, cheeses, olives, and artisan bread paired with their finest whites and rosés
meals.dinner: Dinner at Restaurante Evaristo in Albufeira or equivalent — grilled sea bass with lemon butter, lobster bisque, and a premium Portuguese wine selection

day_by_day.notes: September is one of the best months for wine tourism in the Algarve as harvest season is underway. Ask the estate about participating in a harvest experience if available — a truly memorable and exclusive activity.

day_by_day.morning: Exclusive private boat charter — depart from a nearby marina for a full-morning private yacht excursion along the Algarve's most dramatic coastal stretch between Portimão and Lagos. Anchor in secluded coves accessible only by sea, swim in pristine waters, and snorkel among marine life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Meia Praia, a long and beautiful sandy beach near Lagos, for a relaxed afternoon. Enjoy beach club amenities — premium sun loungers, cold drinks, and light snacks while soaking up the final days of warm Algarve sunshine.
day_by_day.evening: Lagos Old Town Sunset Wine Bar Crawl — Evening Edition: Return to Lagos for a dedicated premium evening wine experience. Visit the best wine bars in the historic center, sampling aged Garrafeiras, premium Alentejo reds, and rare Portuguese varietals with expert guidance.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — fresh fruit salad, granola with local honey, yogurt, and a selection of fine pastries
meals.lunch: On-board yacht lunch — premium catering arranged in advance with the charter company: fresh sashimi, chilled prawns, artisan cheeses, and chilled rosé on deck
meals.dinner: Dinner at Restaurante Adega da Marina in Lagos or equivalent — traditional cataplana de peixe, grilled cuttlefish, and a curated selection of premium Portuguese wines

day_by_day.notes: Book the private yacht charter at least 3–4 days in advance through the resort concierge. Request the captain to anchor at the most secluded coves along the route. Bring snorkeling gear, sunscreen, and a light cover-up for the boat.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning beach experience — revisit your favorite beach from the trip or explore a new one such as Praia do Camilo near Lagos, a hidden gem accessible via a wooden staircase down the cliffs. A perfect farewell morning by the sea.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort for a farewell spa treatment — choose a relaxing full-body massage or a premium hydrotherapy circuit. Spend the final afternoon by the pool or on the beach, savoring every last moment of the Algarve.
day_by_day.evening: Grand farewell dinner at the resort's finest restaurant — a special occasion dinner arranged by the concierge with a premium tasting menu, sommelier wine pairing, and a personalized farewell touch from the resort team.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet breakfast at the resort — order everything you loved during the stay as a final celebration
meals.lunch: Light beachside lunch at the resort's pool bar — grilled fish tacos, fresh salads, and a farewell glass of Algarve rosé
meals.dinner: Premium farewell tasting menu at the resort's signature restaurant — 7-course Algarvian chef's menu with sommelier wine pairing, finishing with a traditional almond and fig tart and a glass of Moscatel de Setúbal

day_by_day.notes: Ask the resort concierge to arrange a special farewell setup — flowers, champagne on arrival at the table, or a personalized menu card as a keepsake. This is the perfect evening to reflect on an extraordinary 13-day journey through the Algarve.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise walk on the beach or a quiet breakfast on your private terrace. Pack and prepare for departure. Arrange late checkout with the resort if your flight allows — most luxury resorts will accommodate this for premium guests.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure time — final coffee and pastéis de nata at a local café in the nearest town, or a last glass of Algarve wine at the resort bar. Private luxury transfer to Faro Airport for your departure flight.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Faro Airport. Carry with you a collection of memories, fine wines purchased from the vineyards, and perhaps a bottle of Quinta dos Vales Reserva to enjoy back home.

meals.breakfast: Final in-suite or terrace breakfast at the resort — keep it light and memorable: fresh fruit, local pastries, and a perfect espresso
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the resort or airport lounge depending on departure time
meals.dinner: N/A — departure day

day_by_day.notes: Arrange the private airport transfer the evening before through the resort concierge. Allow at least 2 hours before your flight for check-in at Faro Airport. Consider purchasing premium Algarvian wines, local honey, artisan ceramics, or cork products as gifts before departing.
